title: A comprehensive analysis of CBER experience with AAV gene therapy IND submissions - Nature Biotechnology
gist: FDA CBER staff analyzed AAV gene therapy IND submissions from 1995 to 2025, finding rapid growth in AAV development over three decades and cataloguing the common reasons for clinical holds that sponsors should address. Only the abstract and figure captions are available (paywalled preview).

themes.theme: Three decades of AAV IND growth

insights.claim: An FDA analysis of Investigational New Drug (IND) submissions from 1995 to 2025 shows rapid growth in adeno-associated virus (AAV) gene therapy development over three decades.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Regulator-side data confirms a sustained, expanding AAV pipeline, supporting demand for AAV vector manufacturing, CDMO capacity and capsid platforms.
insights.quote: reveals a rapid growth in adeno-associated virus (AAV) development over three decades
insights.locator: An analysis of Investigational New Drug

insights.claim: FDA's CBER classified AAV-based gene therapy IND submissions by therapeutic area and by AAV serotype, indicating serotype choice is a tracked regulatory dimension of the AAV pipeline.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Serotype and indication mix data from the regulator can reveal crowded vs. underexplored areas for capsid and indication strategy.
insights.quote: Classification of AAV-based gene therapy IND submissions by therapeutic area and AAV serotype

themes.theme: Clinical hold drivers for AAV programs

insights.claim: FDA reviewers identified recurring categories of clinical hold issues in AAV gene therapy IND submissions, which they say sponsors should consider for successful product development.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Recurring hold causes are a diligence checklist for timeline risk in AAV biotech investments; holds delay trials and burn cash.
insights.quote: highlights common reasons for regulatory holds that should be considered for successful product development
insights.locator: An analysis of Investigational New Drug

insights.claim: The CBER analysis quantifies the frequency of hold issues by category across AAV gene therapy IND submissions, giving a regulator-sourced ranking of where AAV programs most often fail initial review.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: The full paper's hold-category frequencies (not in this preview) are worth obtaining to benchmark sponsor IND readiness.
insights.quote: Frequency of hold issues by category in AAV-based gene therapy IND submissions

insights.claim: The AAV IND analysis was authored entirely by staff of the FDA's Office of Therapeutic Products at CBER, though they state the opinions do not necessarily represent FDA views or policies.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Publication by the reviewing office signals what CBER reviewers scrutinize in AAV filings, a de facto guidance signal for sponsors.
insights.quote: All authors are employed by the US Food and Drug Administration.
